text:
kevin: Trying to deploy the quickstart to Cloudflare Pages and the client-side fetch to /v1/embed returns 403 immediately. REST list models works from the server build, but embedding request from the browser is blocked. Using REDWOOD_API_KEY in the Pages environment. Anyone seen Cloudflare+quickstart oddities? :confused:

devex-bot: Created DEVEX-5768. Please share a minimal repro, browser network logs, and server logs if available.

anna: Cloudflare Pages is an edge/static hosting environment. If you put a workspace/service key into client-side envs it will be treated as untrusted and certain endpoints (streaming, embed generation, auth refresh) reject with 403. Also we intentionally surface a security hint in the console when a key is used client-side, but quickstarts sometimes instruct people to drop REDWOOD_API_KEY in a client .env which is risky.

kevin: Browser console network snippet:
GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embed 403
Response body: {"error":"forbidden","reason":"untrusted_runtime_or_missing_workspace_header"}
Server (Pages) build log: nothing obvious, no server-side function to add headers. I was following quickstart-web-cloudflare example.

liz: If you're hosting purely static pages on Pages, you should never place a workspace key in the browser. Options: 1) Move the embed call into a Pages Function (serverless) that runs with the workspace key and forwards the result to the browser. 2) Use a personal API key for quick demos (not recommended for public sites) or 3) use the CLI proxy locally for dev.

andre: Two follow-ups for DX: - Quickstart change: the Cloudflare Pages example should be updated to include a small Functions handler (api/embed.js) and explicit instructions to set the key as a Pages secret (server-side) not in client env. - SDK change: when a request from a known untrusted runtime hits the embed/stream endpoints with a workspace key, the API should return a clearer error body like {"error":"workspace_key_server_only","hint":"Move call to server-side function or use personal key for local dev: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/quickstarts/cloudflare"}. Right now the error message is generic.

kevin: That would help. Right now the quickstart README just has a note but it's easy to miss. I didn't realize Pages environment variables are injected into both worker and client contexts for some setups.

anna: Agreed. Another small UX improvement: the CLI could scan for REDWOOD_API_KEY in files that are part of the client bundle during `npx @redwood/cli deploy` and warn loudly: "Detected REDWOOD_API_KEY in client-bundled env; this will expose your key publicly and likely cause 403s for protected endpoints. Use a server-side function and set the key as a server secret." We can add that to DEVEX-5768.

liz: For Kevin: quick fix — add a tiny API route in your Pages functions that proxies /v1/embed and set REDWOOD_API_KEY in Pages secrets for that function only. I'll paste a minimal example in the ticket. For the long term we'll update the quickstart and the SDK/API error to be more explicit about untrusted runtimes vs billing gates.

andre: Also adding a console hint: when someone creates a workspace/service key, show a one-time tooltip: "Server-only key. Do not put this in client bundles. Use server functions or create a personal key for local dev." That reduces accidental exposure.

kevin: Thanks all — implemented the function proxy and it fixed the 403. Will attach the repro and rough Pages function to DEVEX-5768 and review any quickstart PRs. Appreciate the guidance!
